newsitem.title: USA: CMS says main Mich. power line still down.
newsitem.headline: CMS says main Mich. power line still down.

text.p: CMS Energy Corp is still rerouting power on its transmission system to skirt a 345 kilovolt (kv) line knocked out of service last week by severe weather, the company said Monday.
"We're rerouting power on adjacent lines, so there is no threat to system integrity. But we're watching it very, very closely," said Jon Hall, a spokesman for the Dearborn, Mich.-based power company.
"Seven towers that were toppled must be replaced from the foundation on up. This is going to take weeks," he said.

CMS's initial damage report listed six towers as destroyed when a line of thunderstorms and tornadoes roared across southeastern Michigan late July 2, playing havoc with distribution lines as well as the region's transmission grid.

The damaged towers support a 345 kv line that runs south from CMS's Karn-Weadock power generating complex in Essexville, Mich., to the Thetford substation, a major interconnect to the neighboring Detroit Edison power grid.
The Thetford facility itself was hard-hit by the storm.
"We still have some repairs to make there. The damage was relatively substantial," Hall said, adding there were no estimates yet on how long the repair work would take.
